## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dutiyapāṭidesanīya* ("Second Pāṭidesanīya") of the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* sets forth a disciplinary training rule concerning the conduct of monks during invitational meals. According to the rule, a monk attending an invitational meal who fails to intervene and instruct a nun to cease directing the distribution of food incurs an offense requiring acknowledgment (*pāṭidesanīya*). The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali. No references to this rule appear in the provided search passages, as all retrieved citations represent spurious non-Buddhist or non-Vinaya matches.

 Cross-tradition parallels are preserved in the Prātimokṣa and Vinayavibhaṅga literature of numerous early Buddhist traditions, including the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsaṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya lineages in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan recensions.
